name: Liu Rongjiao
current_role: Member of the Wen family (actual controllers) of Wens Foodstuff Group, per company filings
profile: Hurun lists Liu Rongjiao (with Wen Junsheng) as a shareholder in Wens Foodstuff Group, China's large pig and chicken producer founded in Guangdong. Wens' 2024 interim report names a '刘容娇' (variant character) among the 10 people making up the Wen family / actual controllers.
interesting_fact: Wens' 2024 interim report defines its actual controller as the 'Wen family', a group of 10 individuals including 刘容娇, rather than a single founder.
notes: Hurun spelling 刘荣娇 vs filing 刘容娇 (likely same person, not confirmed). No public profile; passive family shareholder. Only route is Wens board-secretary office.

name: Zhang Chunhua
current_role: Possibly Chairman, Shenzhen Langhua Investment Holding (朗华集团), a supply-chain services group (link to Hurun 'Brilliant' not confirmed)
profile: Hurun China (2016-17) lists 张春华 of 'Brilliant' in logistics. A Zhang Chunhua chairs Shenzhen Langhua Investment Holding, a supply-chain/logistics group he started after leaving his job in 2006, offering logistics, cross-border compliance and bonded warehousing; whether Langhua is Hurun's 'Brilliant' is unverified.
interesting_fact: Langhua launched Shenzhen's first China-Europe freight train, the 'Langhua Express' to Duisburg, in 2017 after over 600 days of planning (per a 2026 Tencent News profile of Zhang).
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Langhua, Zhang visited Hamburg and Hong Kong to study logistics and supply-chain finance after a meeting with a university supply-chain researcher; he calls his company 'industry's nanny' (工业的保姆).
notes: Identity uncertain: could not confirm that Hurun's 'Brilliant' = 朗华 (Langhua). Verify before outreach. Common name.

name: The Marquess of Salisbury
current_role: 7th Marquess of Salisbury (Robert Gascoyne-Cecil); owner of Hatfield House estate; chairman of the Constitution Reform Group
profile: Robert Gascoyne-Cecil (b. 1946), Eton and Oxford, was a merchant banker, MP for South Dorset (1979-87) and Leader of the House of Lords (1994-97). He succeeded as 7th Marquess in 2003; his wealth is the Hatfield House estate and art collection. He chairs the Constitution Reform Group and Reaction and is a Knight of the Garter (2019).
interesting_fact: Hatfield House, his family seat, was once home to Elizabeth I and was given to the Cecils by James I in exchange for the family's house Theobalds.
deep_cut_fact: In 2020 he published a book on Victorian war artist William Simpson and the Afghan Boundary Commission, the survey that nearly sparked war with Russia in 1885; he also wrote for The Spectator as 'Robert Salisbury'.
notes: Aged 80. Press email is for the Hatfield estate (Gascoyne). Retired from the Lords in 2017; stepped down as Chancellor of University of Hertfordshire Nov 2025.

name: Wang Shouchun
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shandong Xiantan Co. (仙坛股份, SZSE: 002746)
profile: Wang Shouchun (b. June 1962) founded Shandong Xiantan in Yantai in June 2001, building it into a listed integrated broiler-chicken producer; he and his wife Qu Lirong are the actual controllers. He still chairs the company, with filings in 2024-25 showing him chairing board meetings and proposing dividends.
interesting_fact: He and his wife together held 83.68% of Xiantan before its Shenzhen IPO, per the 2013 prospectus.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Xiantan in 2001 he ran a sole-proprietor business and contract farming; a Shandong Agricultural University economics-management graduate, he was named a 'Shandong Rural Star' and an outstanding figure of Muping district's 30 years of reform.
notes: IR email is from the 2013 IPO prospectus; check the latest annual report for the current one. Also vice-chair of the China Animal Agriculture Association's presidium (as of 2013).

name: Gong Xuebin
current_role: Chairman, Longda Group (龙大集团), Laiyang, Shandong (per 2014 IPO documents; current status unverified)
profile: Gong Xuebin (b. 1937) built Longda Group in Laiyang, Shandong, from his post as head of the Laiyang brick and tile factory into a food conglomerate spanning vegetables, frozen foods and pork. With Gong Mingjie he was actual controller of Longda Meat Foodstuff (SZSE: 002726) at its 2014 IPO; that listed firm is now controlled by Lanrun Development.
interesting_fact: A two-time National People's Congress deputy (10th and 11th), he received China's National Model Worker title, the May Day Labour Medal and a lifetime achievement award from the Chinese meat industry.
deep_cut_fact: His early career was as Party secretary and factory director of the Laiyang Brick and Tile Factory before he led Longda; he also served as president of the Shandong Vegetable Association.
notes: Born 1937 (age ~89); no death report found but alive status unconfirmed. Listed Longda Meishi (ST龙大) is now controlled by Lanrun Development (chnfund.com report, 2026), so the Gong family's link is via private Longda Group.

name: Zhou Yaxian
current_role: Chairman and President, Shenguan Holdings (Group) Ltd (HKEX: 0829)
profile: Zhou Yaxian, 66, founded Shenguan, a Wuzhou, Guangxi-based maker of edible collagen sausage casings listed in Hong Kong. She has nearly 46 years in the collagen casing industry and still chairs the group (2025 annual report, signed March 2026), having retired from running the main operating subsidiary in 2024-25.
interesting_fact: She has spent almost her whole career on one product: she worked on trial production of collagen sausage casings at a Wuzhou state meat factory from 1979 before building Shenguan into a casing leader.
deep_cut_fact: She is a co-inventor on four Chinese national patents for collagen casing production methods and equipment, and won a third-class National Science and Technology Progress Award in 1995.
notes: IR email is the company's IR agency (Wonderful Sky Financial Group). Her son Sha Junqi is also an executive director.

name: Jiang Xuezhen
current_role: Chairman, Changzhou Tenglong Auto Parts (腾龙股份, SSE: 603158); Chairman, Sunrise Power (新源动力)
profile: Jiang Xuezhen (b. July 1960) has chaired Changzhou Tenglong Auto Parts, a Shanghai-listed maker of auto thermal-management and fluid piping parts, since 2006. He previously ran a Wujin crane-parts factory (1990-2006). Since 2020 he has also chaired Sunrise Power (新源动力), a hydrogen fuel-cell company.
interesting_fact: Beyond auto parts, he chairs fuel-cell maker Sunrise Power (新源动力) since 2020, a direct link to hydrogen/energy themes.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 1977 at the Anbei farm-machinery plant in Dong'an town, Wujin, then worked at Changzhou Pharmaceutical Factory and Changzhou Mining Machinery Factory before becoming head of the Dong'an crane-parts factory in 1990.
notes: Good energy angle via Sunrise Power fuel cells. Best route: Tenglong board secretary office.
